objective: One Exchange product that lets providers publish usable offerings and customers acquire project access, use shared inference and buy managed Alch execution through a coherent UI/API.
interpretation: MVP-C identifiers are proposed product capability compositions over existing EX-C implementation slices, not newly admitted canonical capability identities.

values.name: Make useful work available
values.outcome: Providers spend less effort turning a project, local engine or authored service into something others can use.

values.name: Obtain and use what was offered
values.outcome: Buyers and callers understand the deliverable and terms, then successfully obtain access or an execution result.

values.name: Run Alch without operating servers
values.outcome: Authors supply supported behavior and Exchange supplies managed operation.

values.name: Participate through software
values.outcome: Agents and applications complete authorized operations through the same contracts as human clients.

values.name: Return with confidence
values.outcome: Clear commitments, bounded costs and recovery make repeat participation practical.

capabilities.name: Participate with explicit authority
capabilities.outcome: A participant can act in permitted scopes with clear separation between their identity, tenant, wallet and provider role.
capabilities.value_mechanism: An existing member can supply or consume without rebuilding identity and authorization for each offering.
capabilities.integration_gap: Unify existing inference, host and purchase identity bindings; choose onboarding and wallet-linking flow.
acceptance: Two independent principals use permitted resources and cannot read, invoke or manage each other’s private resources.
Revocation is checked before an invocation or retained-result replay.
Tenant membership alone grants no invocation; free inference does not require a payment wallet solely to exist.
capabilities.customer_measure: Time from joining to first authorized provider or caller action.
capabilities.counterevidence: Each service requires unrelated accounts or role membership silently grants broad access.
capabilities.owner: Exchange product owner and selected capability owner

capabilities.name: Publish a usable offering
capabilities.actor: Project seller, inference provider or Exchange hosting operator
capabilities.outcome: A provider can publish a versioned offering with its deliverable, eligibility and free/paid terms.
capabilities.value_mechanism: Reusable listing and terms replace per-provider storefront and delivery setup.
capabilities.integration_gap: Build provider publication/editing, typed offering templates and versioned terms; current catalogs are slice-specific.
acceptance: Create project, inference and managed-hosting listings through UI and API.
ARE Static and Full bind distinct package/edition manifests.
Changing price or content creates successor terms; existing accepted requests retain their version.
Selecting free inference produces no payment obligation; paid mode is explicit before invocation.
capabilities.customer_measure: Time and manual work to publish the first usable offering.
capabilities.counterevidence: A listing is only a description and still needs manual arrangements to become usable.
capabilities.owner: Exchange product owner and selected capability owner

capabilities.name: Discover and choose on clear terms
capabilities.outcome: A participant can find an eligible offering and understand what they receive, its terms and current service availability before committing.
capabilities.value_mechanism: One catalog removes repeated interpretation across projects and executable services.
capabilities.integration_gap: Create common catalog/detail/search and projection contracts, preserving type-specific fields.
acceptance: One catalog includes Lab, ARE editions, Craft + Alch, managed hosting and free/paid inference examples.
Discovery separates declared capability, price and last observed availability; unavailable engines are not represented as ready.
Provider addresses, credentials and private project data are absent from public responses.
capabilities.customer_measure: Time from discovery to a correctly understood first request.
capabilities.counterevidence: Buyers need an operator to explain edition contents, price or delivery after selecting an offering.
capabilities.owner: Exchange product owner and selected capability owner

capabilities.name: Acquire a project version
capabilities.outcome: A buyer acquires the selected project edition/version, receives decryptable access, and retains a recoverable purchase record.
capabilities.value_mechanism: Project sale becomes a usable product with exact access and durable recovery.
capabilities.integration_gap: Bind catalog package/edition to the existing purchase flow and shared participant identity; real-money correctness remains unresolved.
acceptance: Purchase the exact listed artifact and edition using independent seller/buyer identities.
Before commitment, expiry refunds; after commitment, payment and membership persist across interrupted delivery.
Unlock grants, pays and commits atomically; retry cannot pay twice.
Client verifies/decrypts and records acknowledgement; Static buyer receives only the selected Static package.
capabilities.customer_measure: Successful purchase-to-first-use rate and recovery completion rate.
capabilities.counterevidence: A successful payment leaves the buyer unable to obtain the promised usable package.
capabilities.owner: Exchange product owner and selected capability owner

capabilities.name: Share and use community inference
capabilities.outcome: A member makes a local engine available and another member invokes it under free or paid terms.
capabilities.value_mechanism: Members can use community models without reproducing each provider’s model installation.
capabilities.integration_gap: Provide member-to-member connectivity, engine publication, controls and paid settlement; current loopback/SSH paths do not prove general connectivity.
acceptance: Two separately operated participant contexts complete JSON and SSE inference.
Provider chooses free or paid and sets allowed access/limits; caller sees terms before invoking.
Disconnects, timeouts and partial streams preserve unknown outcomes; no unsafe retry or zero-usage assumption.
Free requests incur no charge; paid requests follow the chosen metering and settlement contract.
capabilities.customer_measure: Time to first shared invocation; repeat calls across independent providers and callers.
capabilities.counterevidence: Engine sharing still requires an administrator to hand-configure each caller connection.
capabilities.owner: Exchange product owner and selected capability owner

capabilities.name: Buy managed execution of Alch
capabilities.actor: Alch author/customer and Exchange service operator
capabilities.outcome: A customer submits supported Alch source and obtains an operated callable service under agreed hosting terms.
capabilities.value_mechanism: The author supplies behavior while Exchange takes on server operation.
capabilities.integration_gap: Unify upload/build/prepare/activate with hosting agreement, endpoint access, lifecycle and billing; local host primitives do not establish commercial hosting.
acceptance: Submit one supported Alch file, receive build diagnostics, explicitly activate, and call the resulting endpoint.
Observe revision, status, usage and cost; drain/restart with retained state according to the selected contract.
Stop/terminate has an explicit execution and charging cutoff; unknown termination cannot be reported as final.
Unsupported profiles, unauthorized source/secret access and over-limit execution fail with defined outcomes.
capabilities.customer_measure: Time from submitted source to first successful external call and customer server-management effort.
capabilities.counterevidence: Customers must provision or manually repair the hosting environment to use their submitted service.
capabilities.owner: Exchange product owner and selected capability owner

capabilities.name: Control commercial commitments
capabilities.outcome: Participants can agree to a price/budget, distinguish observed usage from money due, and inspect settled or unresolved obligations.
capabilities.value_mechanism: Explicit costs and payment evidence make free sharing and paid participation understandable.
capabilities.integration_gap: Project settlement exists locally; paid inference, hosting metering, prices and platform fee policy need contracts and implementation.
acceptance: Each paid action pins terms, price unit and spending authorization before chargeable work.
A free offering creates no billable obligation.
Duplicate processing cannot create a duplicate obligation or settlement; uncertain chain/provider results remain visible.
Observed usage, provisional charges, finalized payments/refunds and provider earnings have distinct records.
capabilities.customer_measure: Unexpected-charge and disputed-obligation rate; provider ability to reconcile actual earnings.
capabilities.counterevidence: Usage counters are shown as finalized bills or payment is retried on an ambiguous response.
capabilities.owner: Exchange product owner and selected capability owner

capabilities.name: Recover without losing commitment
capabilities.outcome: A participant can identify what happened and safely resume the relevant operation after interruption.
capabilities.value_mechanism: Failures do not force support staff to guess whether payment, execution or access succeeded.
capabilities.integration_gap: Create a common activity/recovery view over typed backend facts, with current authorization and explicit resolution paths.
acceptance: Restart during project delivery, inference execution and hosting activation; show typed committed/pending/unknown state.
Recover a paid artifact without refunding committed ownership; replay only authorized retained JSON inference.
Do not promise stream replay or remote compute cancellation from local disconnect.
Present an operator resolution path where automatic recovery cannot establish the outcome.
capabilities.customer_measure: Recovery success without manual data repair and time to a definitive outcome.
capabilities.counterevidence: The UI guesses success or retries billable work because a network response was lost.
capabilities.owner: Exchange product owner and selected capability owner

capabilities.name: Complete the journey through API or UI
capabilities.outcome: A participant can discover, commit, invoke, inspect and recover using the same authenticated product contracts through either interface.
capabilities.value_mechanism: Software can participate without scripting a human-only checkout or receiving broad operator credentials.
capabilities.integration_gap: Build one coherent application and contract surface; existing CLIs and browser clients are separate.
acceptance: An API client and a browser independently complete each selected journey with equivalent outcomes.
Private signing/decryption remains client-side; application authentication does not transfer wallet or content-key custody.
Stable request identity and typed errors let clients distinguish retryable, rejected and unresolved actions.
capabilities.customer_measure: API task completion and number of manual interventions per journey.
capabilities.counterevidence: Key domain operations exist only as buttons or require access to internal administrator endpoints.
capabilities.owner: Exchange product owner and selected capability owner

capabilities.name: Keep the Exchange operable
capabilities.outcome: Operators can observe availability and outstanding obligations, control services and recover the selected deployment.
capabilities.value_mechanism: Participants can rely on repeat use because the product can be maintained and recovered.
capabilities.integration_gap: Aggregate current service health, queued work, payment/recovery incidents and deployment configuration with scoped operator actions.
acceptance: Observe distinct selected revision, desired state and runtime health.
Exercise bounded overload, restart and backup recovery with exact candidate configuration.
An operator cannot use lifecycle access to obtain participant private keys or plaintext.
capabilities.customer_measure: Time to detect and resolve failed fulfillment; availability during the pilot.
capabilities.counterevidence: A passing demo cannot be restarted or an operator must edit databases to recover commitments.
capabilities.owner: Exchange product owner and selected capability owner

shared_contracts.name: ParticipantBinding
shared_contracts.fields: Principal, tenant/membership, role and explicit wallet/KEP binding references
shared_contracts.invariant: No implicit equality of login, wallet, tenant and KEP identity.

shared_contracts.name: OfferingRevision
shared_contracts.fields: Offering ID, revision, provider, type, public description, fulfillment binding, terms reference, publication status
shared_contracts.invariant: Editing creates a new revision; no buyer receives silently changed bytes.

shared_contracts.name: TermsRevision
shared_contracts.fields: Version, free/paid mode, deliverable, access, price unit/amount/asset when paid, budget rule, deadline, acceptance and recovery policy
shared_contracts.invariant: Fields are type-specific; project grant, inference execution and ongoing hosting have different obligations.

shared_contracts.name: ProjectPackage
shared_contracts.fields: Product, edition, version, artifact digest, KEP version/policy, package manifest and stated rights
shared_contracts.invariant: Static and Full remain different exact deliverables; buying software does not imply hosting or inference entitlement.

shared_contracts.name: EngineOfferingBinding
shared_contracts.fields: Public model/capabilities, private operator connection, access/usage limits and dated availability
shared_contracts.invariant: Provider retains engine operation; secrets never become catalog content.

shared_contracts.name: HostingAgreement
shared_contracts.fields: Customer, supported source revision/profile, plan/terms, deployment reference, access/storage policy and lifecycle
shared_contracts.invariant: Build success does not activate, prove liveness, establish a paid runtime or define charges.

shared_contracts.name: OperationRecord
shared_contracts.fields: Actor/scope, idempotency/request identity, terms and type-specific operation reference, outcome and evidence
shared_contracts.invariant: Common envelope and timeline, separate state machines; unknown is not failure, success or safe retry.

shared_contracts.name: UsageAndSettlement
shared_contracts.fields: Observed usage/provenance, obligation identity, billing rule, settlement/refund references and finality
shared_contracts.invariant: Measured usage, entitlement, debt and settled money are different facts.

milestones.acceptance: Review this capability-to-thesis plan; select remaining commercial and runtime contracts.

milestones.outcome: Build Exchange participation, catalog and workspaces
milestones.acceptance: One UI/API with shared identity and real persisted draft/published listings; representative project, inference and hosting listings.

milestones.outcome: Establish commitments, activity and recovery contracts
milestones.acceptance: Executable contract cases for free/paid usage, hosting lifecycle and project finality; unified activity records with typed outcomes.
End-to-end local valueless purchase through Exchange catalog, identity, checkout, delivery and recovery.
Separate provider and caller connect via selected topology; free and paid-contract cases, usage, disconnect and recovery.
Customer submits supported file, activates endpoint, invokes, observes costs, recovers and terminates under explicit terms.

milestones.outcome: Freeze and test the whole Exchange
milestones.acceptance: One installed candidate passes all three journeys, cross-tenant negatives, restart/overload/recovery and API/UI parity.

milestones.outcome: Run controlled pilot and assess thesis
milestones.acceptance: Exact deployment authorization and operational prerequisites; independent participants; report measured friction, failures, repeat use and payment outcomes.

operational_tasks.causal_blocker: Q4/Q18 must resolve before chargeable paid-service implementation/acceptance; platform fees Q12.
operational_tasks.scope: Exact meters, price units and failure/termination policy; no provider call charged by this plan.

operational_tasks.causal_blocker: Q2/Q17 before host contract and before exposing untrusted customer execution.
operational_tasks.scope: One supported profile first; isolation, quotas, secrets and persistence are explicit.
Separate-host fixture environments support construction; live provider topology needs consent/configuration.

operational_tasks.task: Exact project packages and ARE edition separation
operational_tasks.causal_blocker: Q10/Q16/Q19/Q20 before authentic listings or actual sales.
operational_tasks.scope: Fixtures support M1/M3 local development; all offered release packages require their own closure tests.
Fresh preflight, fee ceiling, key custody and exact authorization; prior balances are historical.
Controlled valueless or Devnet tests do not discharge this blocker.

operational_tasks.task: Live identity, ingress, backups and retention
operational_tasks.causal_blocker: Q3/Q6 before protected live deployment and operational promises.
operational_tasks.scope: Local fixtures support earlier work; configure issuer, TLS, storage recovery and keys explicitly.

runnable_next: Specify the selected identity/offering/terms contracts using concrete examples
Select one supported Alch host composition and managed-hosting lifecycle
Resolve paid inference and hosting units and failure/termination semantics

includes: Shared participant, catalog, activity/recovery and UI/API experience
release_boundary.local_candidate: Deterministic engine fixtures and valueless settlement are allowed but must be labeled.
release_boundary.live_release: No unsupported paid mode may be exposed as working; unresolved Q5 blocks real-money project sales. A reduced pilot requires an explicit scope decision.
